chapter_title: Concerning the Fifty Lord's Days; to what Mysterie
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

---

**¶2:** Within each of these five degrees of external truth that the [GAP-1] primordial celestial will called forth from within itself, there reside five interior faculties. These are to be reckoned together [GAP-2] one with another, these five, and five times [GAP-3] their full number. Yet at the time [GAP-4] the calling-forth of divine truth descended into lower states, the reception of that truth sought to ascend together with it. And the calling-forth of divine truth together with the will's receptive response [GAP-5] constitute twenty-five spiritual faculties in their twenty-five capacities of life, [GAP-6] which are the derivative states proceeding from the celestial will. The divine call and its willing reception were elevated into interior states through these faculties.

**¶3:** Just as their origin, the living celestial will, raised itself into interior states through them, so by these same faculties every other spiritual reality has been ordered in both interior and exterior degrees. They emptied themselves of their own proper spiritual nourishment — that which belongs to them by nature.

**¶4:** And from that state until [GAP-7] the state of the advent of Divine Wisdom made manifest, the glorious influx that came [GAP-8] bearing their spiritual nourishment, which is the [GAP-9] life of the interior spirit — namely, the divine call and its willing reception — [GAP-10] that sustaining truth and good. They released [GAP-11] throughout all these fifty complete states of spiritual process, which [GAP-12] this living truth-and-good suffices to sustain them all. It filled them all with spiritual capacity, with abundance of truth, and with the very life of heaven. Divine wisdom [GAP-13] this living nourishment from the Divine that [GAP-14] was made abundant.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [In eac]h one of these five garments that the [First] Man summoned there are five powers. They shall be counted to the [number of each] other, these five, and five times [five is] their number. However, at the time [when] the summons went down. The answer wished to ascend with it. And the summons with the obedience [constitute] twenty-five characteristics in their twenty-five limbs, [which] are the sons of the Man. The summons and [the obed]ience were raised to the heights through them.
Just as their fa[ther] the living Man raised himself up through them, by these these other ones have set up all things a[bov]e and below. They fasted from their [foo]d, [w]hich is their own.

So, from that time until [the time] of [the adv]ent of Jesus the Splendour, the glorious one who came [from the land of light and gave to them]heir food which is the [life] of sou[l], which is the summons and the obedience [that is] that spiritual food. They rele[ased them throughout] all these fifty days, which [means] this living food suffices for all of them. It filled them all with power and richness and life. Light [is] this living food that [in them] became rich.

fills.explanation: The editor's "First" is correct: "First Man" (Ohrmizd) is the standard Manichaean title for the primordial celestial will who summoned forth the five garments, and the spiritual reading confirms this with "primordial celestial will."

The spiritual reading says "reckoned together one with another," and the text requires a phrase completing "counted to the ___ each other" — "number of each" yields "counted to the number of each other," expressing the mutual reckoning of the five powers within each garment.
The passage establishes 5×5=25; "five times five is their number" completes the arithmetic statement and matches the spiritual reading's "five times their full number."
A standard temporal connector is required: "at the time when the summons went down" mirrors the spiritual reading's "at the time the calling-forth descended."

The editor's "constitute" is confirmed: the summons and obedience together form/constitute the twenty-five characteristics, matching the spiritual reading's "constitute twenty-five spiritual faculties."

The editor's "which" is confirmed: a relative pronoun is needed to connect the twenty-five limbs to the identification as "sons of the Man," matching the spiritual reading's "which are the derivative states."
The editor's "the time" is confirmed: "until the time of the advent" is the standard Kephalaia temporal construction, matching the spiritual reading's "until the state of the advent."

fills.fill: from the land of light and gave to them
fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says Jesus came "bearing their spiritual nourishment"; in the Kephalaia's natural register, Jesus the Splendour descends from the land of light and delivers sustenance — filling approximately two manuscript lines and ending naturally before "their food."
The spiritual reading identifies this as "the life of the interior spirit"; "life of soul" is the natural-register equivalent, identifying the food as the animating life-principle of the soul.

The spiritual reading uses an appositional dash equating the summons-and-obedience with the sustaining food; "that is" provides the natural-register explanatory connector identifying the summons and obedience as that spiritual food.

The spiritual reading says "They released throughout all these fifty complete states"; completing "released them throughout" indicates the liberation/sustenance of the twenty-five faculties across the entire fifty-day period, connecting to the prior fasting motif.

A connective is needed between the relative "which" and the explanatory clause; "means" yields "which means this living food suffices for all of them," expressing that the fifty-day sustenance demonstrates the food's sufficiency.

The spiritual reading identifies Divine wisdom with this living nourishment; "Light is this living food" establishes the correspondential identity between Light (divine wisdom) and the spiritual food, a standard Kephalaia equation.

The spiritual reading says the nourishment "was made abundant"; "in them" specifies that the living food became rich/abundant within the recipients, completing the theme of interior spiritual enrichment through the food's reception.
